review_notes: I read the whole file and the definitions it relies on: `translatedTruncLE_zero` (which is @[simp]) and `degree_translatedTruncLE_eq` in Derivative.lean. I also searched the ConwayRefinement tree for other uses of `degree_translatedTruncLE_eq` and for existing specialised lemmas. The file has no simp attributes of its own, and I found no loops or competing rules. Leaving `degree_translatedTruncLE_eq` (an `if` expansion) out of the simp set looks deliberate and sensible. The only issue is the missing side-condition-specialised rewrite lemmas next to it. The `_of_notMem_closedSupport` one exists but sits in CofactorInduction.lean, which imports this file, so this file cannot use it. I did not run Lean, so the suggestion is untested. Its benefit is moderate, and I am unsure whether the maintainers would want the `@[simp]` attribute rather than plain lemmas.

findings.problem: The only rewrite interface for the degree of a translated truncation is `degree_translatedTruncLE_eq`, which unfolds to an `if` on `γ ∈ closedSupport`. It is rightly not simp, because it would expand every `ν (translatedTruncLE γ b)`. The consequence is that every use must do `rw [degree_translatedTruncLE_eq, ite_eq_left h]` or `ite_eq_right h` by hand. This file does so twice, at lines 136 and 143, and it also hand-unfolds `NatOrdinal.val_of` and `cantorBendixsonRank_eq` to compare with `β.val`. The same two-step rewrite recurs in PWOAddition.lean, LowerTruncationDegree.lean, TranslatedTruncationInterpolation.lean and CofactorInduction.lean. The membership-conditioned forms that would normalise these goals do not exist at the base level. The `notMem` form `degree_translatedTruncLE_eq_bot_of_notMem_closedSupport` is only defined later, in CofactorInduction.lean. That file imports this one, so it cannot be used here.
findings.proposed_change: Next to `degree_translatedTruncLE_eq` in Derivative.lean, add two side-condition lemmas: `degree_translatedTruncLE_of_mem_closedSupport (h : γ ∈ b.closedSupport) : ν (translatedTruncLE γ b) = ↑(NatOrdinal.of (b.cantorBendixsonRank γ))`, and the `notMem` version (move the CofactorInduction lemma there). Tag them @[simp]. They are conditional rewrites, so simp can discharge the hypothesis from the local context or with `simp [hxm]`, and they cannot expand unconditionally or cycle. Then `hu'` reduces to `simp [hxm]`-style rewriting in each branch, and the other call sites can drop the `rw [..., ite_eq_*]` boilerplate.
findings.benefit: The `ite` stays out of the goal, goals are normalised to the rank or ⊥ only when membership is known, and the repeated manual unfold-and-resolve-`ite` proof pattern disappears from this file and its siblings.
